name: Crawl
description: Documentation-only (#1959) — `crawl` carries NO Task/Step graph. `darkmux mission launch crawl` is routed by literal config id in `mission_launch::launch`, BEFORE this document (or any mission-config document) is ever loaded: its Task/Step graph is computed at RUN TIME from a resolved crawl plan, one Task per (source, rule-set) grouping, built fresh from whatever the `workspace`/`rules`/`source`+`rule` inputs below resolve to on THIS invocation — there is nothing static to declare ahead of time the way `coder-phase`'s fixed worktree->coder->verify chain or `review`'s fixed bundle->probe->dedup->judge->verify->synthesis chain can. This file exists purely so `mission config list`/`mission config show crawl` can enumerate crawl's inputs for a curious operator; editing `phases` here has NO effect on what a real crawl launch does — see `src/crawl_launch.rs`'s own module doc for the real launcher.

inputs.name: workspace
inputs.description: Path to a workspace spec JSON (darkmux_crew::workspace_spec::WorkspaceSpec) — named sources + include/exclude filters + optional rule-id defaults. Required unless `source` is given for a one-shot crawl. The spec's own `rules` array is the default rule binding when `--param rules=` is absent.

inputs.name: rules
inputs.description: Comma-separated rule ids to crawl with. Wins over the workspace spec's own `rules` array when given; wins over a one-shot `--param rule=` too.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: One-shot crawl: a single path or git URL, synthesizing a one-source workspace spec in memory (no spec file needed). Requires `--param rule=` (a one-shot crawl runs exactly one rule). Mutually exclusive with `workspace` in practice — when both are given, `workspace` wins.

inputs.name: rule
inputs.description: The single rule id to run against `--param source=` in the one-shot path. Ignored when `--param rules=` or a workspace spec's own `rules` array supplies a binding instead.

inputs.name: plan
inputs.description: Path to a previously-written plan JSON (`--param plan_out=` from an earlier `--dry-run`, or a plan a prior run left behind) — skips re-planning and dispatches straight from it. Bails loudly if the plan's `workspace` name or any resolved source's sha/tree has drifted since it was written.

inputs.name: units
inputs.description: Comma-separated unit ids to run, filtering the resolved plan down to exactly those. Bails on an unknown id.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: Cap the number of units dispatched this run (after any `--param units=` filter). `0` selects nothing and completes cleanly — the run's own honest no-op.

inputs.name: no_fetch
inputs.description: Resolve sources against the mirror as-is, without `git fetch`ing first — fully offline against whatever's already mirrored. A `git` source with no mirror yet REFUSES instead of cloning; a `path` source's first clone is local-filesystem-only and is exempt.

inputs.name: dry_run
inputs.description: (#1959) The generic `mission launch --dry-run` flag, injected as `dry_run=true` by the CLI layer — never set by hand. Resolves + plans (everything a real launch does, so a missing/invalid input still bails the same way), then prints the plan table and mints NOTHING: no mission, no flow records, no dispatch. Writes nothing to disk unless `plan_out` is also given.

inputs.name: plan_out
inputs.description: (#1959) Path to write the full plan JSON to, on a `--dry-run` invocation. Absent means a dry run writes nothing — read-only by default.

inputs.name: resume
inputs.description: (#2114 follow-up) A PRIOR crawl mission id to resume. Pass the EXACT SAME `workspace`/`rules`/`source`/`rule`/`plan`/`units`/`limit`/`no_fetch` inputs as the original launch (minus this key itself) — the launch REFUSES OUTRIGHT, before minting anything, if this run's inputs fingerprint differs from the prior mission's own recorded one, since crawl re-plans and re-fetches on every launch and different inputs can shift which unit id means what. NOTE: `units`/`limit` are applied to THIS run's own selection BEFORE the resume filter runs (select first, then skip/resume/fresh each selected unit) — a resume with a narrower `limit` than the original never revisits units outside the first N of THIS run's selection, even if they were part of the original plan. With matching inputs, each of THIS run's selected units is looked up in the prior mission's `envelope.json` by unit id AND matching source/rule (a shifted positional id with a different source/rule is treated as never having run): completed (`result: "stop"`) is skipped entirely; aborted with a checkpoint at its recorded `out_dir` resumes from it (`--resume`, at most one re-executed tool call); anything else (no usable checkpoint, or no record at all — the launcher process itself died before recording one) is re-run fresh. Bails loudly if the named mission or its `envelope.json` can't be found/read.
